title: EEOC opens antisemitism probe into NEA, Brandeis Center says
summary: The center’s complaint alleges the teachers union didn’t specify Jews as the primary victims of the Holocaust, among other things.

title: 7 stories on new and recent grads in the labor market
summary: Generation Z interns are increasingly citing old-school, hands-on experiences as among the most valuable workplace exposures they can have.

title: Workday can’t shake California AI discrimination claims
summary: Because Workday is headquartered in California, a “sufficient nexus” exists to apply the state law even to nonresidents, a federal judge determined.

title: Onboarding begins even before a candidate’s first interview, one HR pro says
summary: Lindsay Gainor, a vice president of HR at ServiceMaster Brands, shares onboarding tips to help ensure new hires stay past the one-year mark.

title: SHRM’s Alex Alonso believes human skills have a place in the future of work
summary: The SHRM26 annual conference gave HR professionals a wealth of AI advice, including insight on what roles humans play going forward.

title: Remote workers represent ‘a disproportionate share’ of unemployed adults, Gallup says
summary: While artificial intelligence wasn’t cited as the reason for layoffs, its impact was often evident in more subtle ways, the report noted.

title: In the AI age, how can HR stay human?
summary: Instead of artificial intelligence, HR pros should focus on “authentic intelligence” — human intuition, in other words, author and leadership expert Alison Jones said.

title: SHRM CEO: HR faces ‘extinction’ and has ‘lost the plot’ on the future of work
summary: The new CHRO, dubbed the Chief Work Officer, will juggle robots, AI and humans and — above all — take back the profession from those who don’t see its value, Johnny Taylor said.

title: 4th Circuit strips class certification in Anheuser-Busch lawsuit, finding members too different
summary: Evidence showed prospective class members performed substantially different tasks and were subject to different legal standards, the court said.

title: 9th Circuit reverses sexual orientation bias ruling in favor of Christian ministry
summary: A dissenting judge wrote that the decision represented part of a “disturbing path” with respect to religious freedom protections.
